text:
chris_acme: Hey team — we started seeing 429s and ~200-500ms tail latency spikes on our Dedicated pool r-dedicated-12 around 02:15 UTC. Could be related to recent long-context usage. Customers hit errors in bursts.

jess_support: thanks for reporting, chris. Can you share a sample request id or a timestamp window? any recent config changes on your side? :eyes: 

chris_acme: sample req ids: req_0a7b2c, req_0a7b2d. Spike window ~02:15–02:45. No config changes from our app. We did start a new long-running prompt job that streams 32k tokens around 02:10.

jess_support: copying eng + oncall — @alin_eng @priya_sre. We'll pull metrics and kvcache stats.

alin_eng: pinged. chris — can you run `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests/req_0a7b2c` and paste the headers/body? trying to correlate 429s to kvcache errors.

chris_acme: pasted output: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 02:18:12 GMT
x-rw-request-id: req_0a7b2c
x-rw-node: r-dedicated-12-node-5
retry-after: 3

{"error":{"message":"request throttled: kvcache_pressure","code":429}}
```

alin_eng: thanks. initial look at our side: kvcache eviction rate shot up on r-dedicated-12 at 02:12 UTC. Memory fragmentation on slab0 increased, free segments dropped from 124 -> 18 in ~3m. Looks like one tenant produced many large contexts and prevented effective coalescing.

priya_sre: posting kvcache summary from monitoring (trimmed):
```
# r-dedicated-12 kvcache metrics (02:00-02:30 UTC)
evictions/sec: baseline 0.4 -> peak 56
kv_hits: 91% -> 60%
fragmentation_index: 0.12 -> 0.63
slab_free_segments[s0]: 124 -> 18
alloc_failures: 0 -> 47
```

alin_eng: also seeing frequent `alloc_coalesce()` retries and background defrag unable to keep up because that node was pinned at 98% GPU util by the long-context jobs. Autoscale didn't add new nodes because the policy requires 2 consecutive min-slo breaches — thresholding meant first few spikes were ignored.

jess_support: summarizing for chris: kvcache fragmentation + heavy long-context streams from at least one tenant caused sustained evictions and alloc failures, resulting in request throttling (429). We're escalating to a short-term mitigation and a longer-term change.

chris_acme: what's the mitigation? this is affecting live users.

alin_eng: mitigation plan (short-term):
- throttle that noisy tenant at the routing layer (rate limit by tenant id)
- trigger immediate slab defrag job on r-dedicated-12 (`sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kvcache-defrag --pool r-dedicated-12 --aggressive`)
- bump pool burst capacity (add 1 hot node) while defrag runs

priya_sre: executed defrag job at 02:36 UTC (logged). Also temporarily enabled tenant rate limit for chris_acme: tenant_qps=8.

deploy-bot: deploy started: add-capacity r-dedicated-12 +1-hot-node by priya_sre at 02:39 UTC.

priya_sre: after defrag + +1 node: slab_free_segments[s0] rose to 108, fragmentation_index down to 0.18, evictions/sec back to 0.6. 429s dropped to baseline. Monitoring in watch. :white_check_mark:

chris_acme: confirmed — errors stopped ~02:42, tail latencies returning to normal. Thanks. Any recommended config changes to avoid recurrence?

alin_eng: long-term recommendations:
- enable tenant-level soft preemption for long-context jobs (we'll roll config flag `tenant.preempt_longctx=true` behind an opt-in beta)
- improve coalescing heuristics and background defrag priority when alloc_failures > 5/min
- adjust autoscale policy: reduce consecutive-slo-window to 1 for high-priority pools or add a reactive spike detector that triggers immediate burst capacity on sharp eviction deltas
- expose kvcache fragmentation alerts to customers (so they can pause workloads)

jess_support: filed internal ticket RW-INC-2026-394 (support) and linked to infra ticket RW-ENG-2026-1183 for autoscale policy change + kvcache improvements.

chris_acme: is there any billing impact or token loss? we saw a couple of retries on our side.

alin_eng: no token loss server-side; throttled requests returned 429 before token consumption beyond request. If you retried, they consumed new tokens. We'll waive overruns in this maintenance window — I'll loop billing.

jess_support: billing notified. @priya_sre can you confirm waiver with finance?

priya_sre: finance looped — they'll review final metrics and waive burst charges for the window 02:10–02:50 for customer acme-inc.

chris_acme: appreciated. any follow-up actions we should expect?

alin_eng: timeline:
- today: hotfixes — autoscale spike detector prototyped (RW-ENG-2026-1183) and a kvcache defrag tuning patch deployed to staging; tenant preemption feature scoped.
- 1 week: roll autoscale reactive spike detector to production behind flag for dedicated pools.
- 3 weeks: coalescing heuristic improvements + metrics export for fragmentation.

jess_support: closing the immediate support thread but keeping tickets open. chris_acme if you see any reoccurrence ping here or DM. :handshake:

chris_acme: will do. thanks all for the quick turnaround. :pray: 

sre-bot: alert resolved: kvcache_pressure on r-dedicated-12 cleared at 02:44 UTC (incident id ir-2026-993).
